plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Bare branches turn into clouds of blush-white, almond-scented blossoms. Petals drift down like confetti and carpet paths and water in pink. Crowds gather each spring to see them around Washington's Tidal Basin.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to early April around Washington, D.C., where peak bloom usually falls in the last days of March or the first days of April
plants.location: Tidal Basin, Washington, D.C., USA (originally from Japan)
plants.funFact: Yoshino cherries are a cultivated hybrid. The first trees at the Tidal Basin were a 1912 gift from Tokyo, and the blossoms open before the leaves, which makes the display look even denser.

plants.name: Nerine sarniensis
plants.description: Spidery, glittering crimson-scarlet flowers rise on bare stems from the Cape's autumn fynbos. The petals shimmer as if dusted with gold. They flower while the bulbs are leafless, and the display lights up rocky mountain slopes.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (March to April) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The 'Guernsey' name probably comes from a shipwreck legend. Bulbs washed ashore on the Channel Island of Guernsey and took root there. They are in fact native to South Africa.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A Himalayan giant that bursts into huge, goblet-shaped pink blooms on bare winter branches. In mild Cornish gardens it often flowers from mid to late March. A mature tree in full flower is a spectacular sight against the spring sky.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late March in the mild gardens of Cornwall; late winter to early spring in its native range
plants.location: Cornwall, England, UK (native to the Himalayas)
plants.funFact: Magnolias are among the oldest flowering plants. Their blooms evolved before bees existed, so they are sturdy enough to be pollinated by beetles.

plants.name: Eschscholzia californica
plants.description: Silky, satin-textured cups of molten orange blaze across hillsides, and in wet years whole valleys turn gold. The petals close on cloudy days and at night, then open again in the sun.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-March to early May in the Antelope Valley, with peak display varying by rainfall
plants.funFact: California's state flower. In wet winters its blooms can be so dense that the 'superbloom' is visible from space.
